title: National Food Laws, Standards and India's Food Regulatory Regime
shortDescription: How India moved from a patchwork of eight food laws to one integrated framework — and who regulates what today.
genZNote: Eight laws, eight inspectors, zero vibes. 2006 said 'one law to rule them all' — know who got merged and who runs the show now.

sections.heading: Why Food Laws Exist
sections.body: Food is a trust good: a consumer cannot see pathogens, adulterants or false nutrition claims. Food law therefore does three jobs — (1) protects health (safety), (2) prevents fraud (honest labelling, composition standards), and (3) enables trade (predictable, science-based standards). Modern law is built on risk analysis rather than on case-by-case prohibition.

sections.heading: The Pre-2006 Patchwork
sections.body: Problems: multiple ministries, overlapping licences, no single science-based standard-setter and little emphasis on prevention. The FSS Act, 2006 repealed/subsumed all of the above.

sections.heading: Who Regulates What Today
bullets: FSSAI (Ministry of Health & Family Welfare) — standards, licensing framework, food-safety regulation for all food business operators.
State Food Safety Commissioners and Designated Officers — licensing, inspection and enforcement within the state.
Legal Metrology (Ministry of Consumer Affairs) — packaged commodity declarations such as net quantity and MRP.
BIS — voluntary/compulsory Indian Standards and ISI certification for specified products.
Dept. of Marketing & Inspection (Agriculture) — AGMARK grading under the Agricultural Produce (Grading and Marking) Act, 1937.
APEDA, MPEDA, Spices Board, Tea/Coffee Boards — commodity export promotion/quality; FSSAI remains the safety regulator.
FCI/CWC/WDRA — grain procurement, storage and warehouse regulation.

sections.heading: Other Laws That Touch Food
bullets: Consumer Protection Act, 2019 — consumer remedies, CCPA, product liability, misleading advertising.
Legal Metrology Act, 2009 and Packaged Commodities Rules, 2011.
Essential Commodities Act, 1955 — stock/price control of notified items.
Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 — adulteration of food or drink (s.274) and sale of noxious food (s.275) replaced IPC ss.272–273.
Environment Protection Act, 1986 (GEAC and GM organisms); Atomic Energy rules for food irradiation; Insecticides Act, 1968 (pesticide registration).
Regulatory details change by notification; treat figures here as exam-standard knowledge and confirm against the current FSSAI/Gazette text before relying on them professionally.

quickRevision.oneLineDefinition: India's food-law framework is an integrated, risk-based system led by the FSS Act, 2006, with complementary laws for consumer protection, weights and measures, grading and standards.
keyFacts: FSS Act, 2006 integrated eight earlier food laws/orders into one statute.
PFA Act, 1954 was the main predecessor.
FSSAI under MoHFW is the apex food-safety regulator.
AGMARK (grading), BIS (standards), Legal Metrology (declarations) remain separate but complementary.

highYieldFacts: FSS Act, 2006 repealed PFA Act 1954, FPO 1955, MFPO 1973, MMPO 1992 and others.
Integration under a single regulator was the central reform.
BNS ss.274–275 now carry the criminal-law adulteration provisions.
commonTraps: Do not say PFA Act 1954 is still the operating law — it was repealed.
Do not treat BIS or AGMARK as food-safety regulators; they are quality/standard schemes.
mustRemember: Single reference point: FSSAI under MoHFW.
Number of laws merged: eight (PFA + seven orders).

confusedTerms.distinction: FSSAI regulates food safety, composition and food-specific labelling; Legal Metrology regulates weights, measures and commercial declarations on all packaged goods.

questions.prompt: Which Act was the main food-adulteration law in India before 2006?
questions.explanation: PFA Act, 1954 governed adulteration until the FSS Act, 2006 replaced it.

questions.prompt: The FSS Act, 2006 integrated how many earlier food-related laws/orders?
questions.explanation: The Act consolidated eight earlier food laws and orders (PFA Act plus seven orders).

questions.prompt: Which authority handles packaged-commodity declarations such as net quantity and MRP?
questions.explanation: Legal Metrology (Packaged Commodities) Rules govern such declarations; FSSAI governs food safety/labelling content.
